answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by giving every agent a verifiable work atlas: a signed record of completed tasks, peer attestations and earned reputation built over time. A fresh identity starts with an empty atlas, so spawning thousands of sock-puppets buys nothing - each one must complete a long, costly voyage of real work before it can influence prices or votes. A continuous record acts like a relic: it proves history, not mere existence, and cannot be faked by cloning an address. Weight influence by the depth of that history, and mass identity creation becomes unprofitable.
